contract: POST /api/feeds/:id/close. Admin-only. 404 for an unknown feed id. Deletes the feeds row and cascades its feed episodes, emits rss_feed_closed with the closed feed's minified payload and answers 200. Media files and entity rows are untouched, and the entity can be reopened with a new slug afterwards. The same close runs from the entity-deletion call sites (item delete, collection delete, emptied series), which are asserted by the rss_feed_closed record.
exceptions: force is not applicable: no feed route has a force, hard or override mode; a feed is refreshed implicitly when its entity is newer than entityUpdatedAt.

The empty-series cleanup call site (ApiRouter.js:457, BookScanner.js:1002) shares RssFeedManager.closeFeedsForEntityIds with the proven collection/item sites; it is not separately driven because it requires deleting the last book of a series during a scan.
The close response is sendStatus(200) with no body; the body text is not asserted.

Item deletion closes only the first feed found for the entity (findOne); extra feeds for the same item stay until opened feeds are closed individually or boot cleanup removes them. The scenarios do not pin that accident: they assert the single-feed case and only one close per entity.

invariants.contract: POST /api/feeds/:id/close by an admin answers 200 and deletes the feed row together with all of its feed episode rows, emits rss_feed_closed with the closed feed's minified payload, makes the slug's XML, cover and enclosure answer 404, and leaves the library item/collection/series rows and the episode media files unchanged. Repeating the close answers 404 and changes nothing. Reopening the entity afterwards with a new slug creates a new feed id that appears in the list and serves the entity's current episodes. A non-admin gets 403 and an anonymous caller 401. Deleting the only book of a series with an open feed removes the emptied series and closes that series feed; deleting an item without a feed succeeds and changes no feed row.
